content.user_title: Assess work readiness with quality gates
content.value_statement: Unclear requirements and repeated failed attempts can waste implementation time. This skill provides structured checks, escalation templates, and evidence-based stop conditions before work proceeds.
actual_capabilities: Scores task complexity on a five-level scale using scope, dependencies, estimates, and unknowns.
Identifies unanswered critical questions and missing dependencies before implementation begins.
Provides pass, warning, and blocked gate decisions with documented reasons.
Tracks repeated failed attempts and prepares an escalation message after three attempts.
Breaks Level 4 and Level 5 work into smaller subtasks with dependencies and acceptance criteria.
Supplies requirements and API-contract checklists for feature planning.
limitations: It provides guidance and templates; it does not inspect repositories or execute tests.
Complexity scores and estimates depend on the accuracy of supplied task information.
The three-attempt escalation threshold may need adjustment for a specific team or task.
It does not replace stakeholder decisions, security reviews, or technical approval.

use_cases.title: Plan a feature before coding
use_cases.description: Use the pre-task gate to identify unknowns, dependencies, and acceptance criteria for a new feature.

use_cases.title: Escalate persistent blockers
use_cases.description: Record failed approaches and prepare a focused request for guidance after repeated unsuccessful attempts.

use_cases.title: Improve delivery readiness
use_cases.description: Apply the requirements checklist and task breakdown template before committing a team to complex work.

prompt_templates.title: Check a simple task
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a quality gate for this task: update the account settings page text. List assumptions, dependencies, complexity, and a pass, warning, or blocked decision.

prompt_templates.title: Clarify a feature request
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this feature request with the requirements completeness checklist: add saved searches. Identify critical unanswered questions and ask only the questions needed to proceed.

prompt_templates.title: Break down complex work
prompt_templates.prompt: Rate this task and create a gated execution plan: migrate authentication to a new provider. Break any Level 4 or 5 work into subtasks with dependencies, acceptance criteria, and evidence checks.

prompt_templates.title: Escalate a blocked task
prompt_templates.prompt: I have tried three approaches to fix this failing integration test. Create a stuck-task escalation with attempt history, the current blocker, targeted questions, and recommended next actions.

output_examples.input: Assess a request to add CSV export to the reports page.
output: Open questions: export size limit, permission rules, and file format details
Next action: confirm assumptions and define acceptance tests before implementation.

output_examples.input: Review a Level 5 request to replace the billing system.
output: Reason: high complexity without a breakdown
Suggested phases: requirements, migration design, provider integration, verification, and rollout
Evidence required: passing integration tests and migration validation.

best_practices: Run a short gate check before every task and a full check before Level 3 or higher work.
Record assumptions and convert unresolved critical questions into explicit requests for guidance.
Use test and build evidence to confirm completion rather than relying only on implementation status.
anti_patterns: Do not start complex work when critical requirements or dependencies remain unknown.
Do not repeat the same failed approach without recording the result and changing strategy.
Do not treat a blocked gate as permission to continue without resolving the blocker.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It provides quality-gate workflows for assessing readiness before implementation and escalating blocked work.

faq.question: Does it execute tests or inspect my project?
faq.answer: No. It provides prompts, checklists, and templates. You must supply project facts and test evidence.

faq.question: When should I use a quality gate?
faq.answer: Use one before starting work, when requirements are unclear, after repeated failures, or before complex planning.

faq.question: What causes a blocked decision?
faq.answer: Common causes include more than three unanswered critical questions, missing dependencies, repeated failed attempts, or complex work without a plan.

faq.question: How are complexity levels assigned?
faq.answer: The skill uses scope, estimated effort, file count, dependencies, and unknowns to assign a level from one to five.

faq.question: Can teams change the gate thresholds?
faq.answer: Yes. Treat the thresholds as a starting point and adapt them to the team process, project risk, and delivery constraints.
